result.title: PORA: Learning When More Reasoning Pays Off for LLM Agents
result.summary: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. During training, \method{} completes the task twice from each selected state, once with a short reasoning allowance and once with a long allowance, and compares their final quality and total processing to estimate when longer reasoning is valuable. During inference, a controller weighs this estimate against learned prices on remaining-budget pressure and chooses either short or long reasoning without running both alternatives. We evaluate PORA across application, memory, code, retail, and mathematics tasks, achieving strong results across all settings. On BFCL memory, it exceeds the strongest existing method by 17.4--32.9 percentage points. Within the same agent, it matches or exceeds always using long reasoning on code and mathematics with 50.6% fewer actor tokens and 31.2% fewer model requests, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PORA，从同一交互状态分别执行一次短推理和一次长推理，用两者最终质量与总开销比较来估计长推理的下游价值，并在推理时由控制器结合剩余预算压力，直接选择短或长推理而不必并行跑两条路径。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同状态配对比较长短推理、再对预算压力定价」的监督与决策方式，可供核查为 LVR 中是否延长 latent 计算、何时停止（THINK/STOP 的收益-成本权衡）提供借鉴；但原文为纯文本 agent，未涉及视觉证据筛选与内部状态表示。
